name: Navratri Pilgrimage at Vaishno Devi
description: Massive pilgrimage surge at Mata Vaishno Devi shrine during the nine-day Navratri festival. The shrine area is decorated with vibrant floral arrangements and colorful lights. Special Maha Yagya ceremonies with Vedic hymns are performed. Attracts hundreds of thousands of devotees during both Chaitra Navratri (Mar-Apr) and Sharad Navratri (Sep-Oct).
significance: One of the most significant Hindu pilgrimage festivals in India. Vaishno Devi is one of the 51 Shakti Peeths. Pilgrims trek to the cave shrine 5,200 ft above Katra town.

name: Lolab Winter Festival
description: A two-day celebration of Kashmiri culture held at Kariwan in Devar Lolab. Features traditional folk music, snow volleyball, skiing, dance performances, local handicraft displays, and culinary delights. Attracts thousands of visitors for music performances, heritage walks, and nature experiences.
significance: Celebrates winter season and showcases scenic splendor of Lolab Valley. Promotes Lolab as a premier winter-tourism destination and generates economic activity for local businesses.

name: Alchi Gustor Festival
description: Sacred masked dance festival held at Alchi Monastery. Features traditional Cham dances performed by monks in elaborate costumes, along with cultural events and spiritual rituals.
significance: Important Buddhist festival in the Alchi monastery tradition, showcasing Ladakh's Tantric Mahayana Buddhist heritage. The masked dances depict spiritual themes central to Ladakh's monastic calendar.

name: Kargil Vijay Diwas
description: National observance commemorating India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War. At Drass War Memorial, wreath-laying ceremonies, patriotic events, and cultural programs are held annually. The memorial features the Captain Manoj Pandey gallery celebrating the Param Vir Chakra awardee.
significance: Honors soldiers who died during Operation Vijay. The Drass War Memorial has become a major landmark and tourist attraction in Western Ladakh, drawing over 125,000 visitors annually.

name: Likir Dosmochey (Stromochey) Festival
description: One of the most important monastic festivals in Ladakh held at Likir Monastery. Features vibrant masked dances (Cham) performed by monks in elaborate costumes depicting the triumph of good over evil. Sacred rituals and votive offerings (Dosmochey) are performed to ward off evil spirits.
significance: Marks the end of the harsh winter season and Tibetan New Year celebrations. Celebrates the Gelugpa Buddhist tradition at Likir, one of the major gompa festivals in Ladakh. Named the Festival of the Scapegoat.

name: Balti Spangang Festival
description: Two-day Balti Literary and Cultural Festival celebrating Balti heritage and culture. Features traditional folk music, soul-stirring Balti Ghazals, heritage walks through Bogdang Old Village and Farol Turtuk, and visits to the Balti Heritage House Museum. Organized jointly by Ladakh Academy of Art, Culture & Languages.
significance: Preserves and celebrates Balti cultural heritage. Turtuk is the northernmost village in India accessible to civilians, home to the unique Balti ethnic minority with their own language, customs, and traditions.

name: Nowruz (Balti New Year)
description: Balti New Year celebration marked by special dishes, egg painting, egg fights, singing, dancing around fires, and traditional music. Believed that the winner of the egg fight will have good luck during the year.
significance: Ancient Persian-Balti spring festival celebrating renewal and prosperity. Unique to the Balti community in Turtuk, reflecting their historical cultural connections beyond the Indian border.
